CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Batu Bara Regency.

2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Batu Bara.
5. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Child protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
13. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
14. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
15. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to the region of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
18. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.

19. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
20. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service unit services in reports/providing complaint handling services, health services, Social Rehabilitation, enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

REGENT OF BATU BARA

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE [

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 16

1. In providing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:a. establish family partners at the Village/Sub-district level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of the rights of Women and Children ' independently;
c. provide first aid to victims; andd. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER VI

MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS

Article 9

MSS for Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence include services for:
a. handling complaints/reports of victims of violence against women and children;
b. health services for women and children victims of violence;
c. Social rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; d. law enforcement and legal aid for women and children victims of violence; ande. repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

S'

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over > the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of service delivery for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND

CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation regulates protection efforts for women and child victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and child victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I

CHAPTER III

< rr

Article 12

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities » for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII

REPORTING

Article 13

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

CHAPTER XII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 17

In the event that the IPU as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1) has not been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the duties and functions of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Batu Bara Regency.

2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Batu Bara.
5. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Child protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
13. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
14. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
15. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to the region of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
18. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.

19. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
20. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service unit services in reports/providing complaint handling services, health services, Social Rehabilitation, enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

Article 12

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities » for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over > the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 16

1. In providing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:a. establish family partners at the Village/Sub-district level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of the rights of Women and Children ' independently;
c. provide first aid to victims; andd. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation regulates protection efforts for women and child victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and child victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Batu Bara Regency.

2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Batu Bara.
5. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Child protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
13. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
14. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
15. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to the region of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
18. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.

19. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
20. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service unit services in reports/providing complaint handling services, health services, Social Rehabilitation, enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER XII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 17

In the event that the IPU as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1) has not been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the duties and functions of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

CHAPTER VI

MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS

Article 9

MSS for Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence include services for:
a. handling complaints/reports of victims of violence against women and children;
b. health services for women and children victims of violence;
c. Social rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; d. law enforcement and legal aid for women and children victims of violence; ande. repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

S'

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 15

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over > the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of service delivery for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER VIII

REPORTING

Article 13

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 11

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 14

Funding for the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence shall be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation regulates protection efforts for women and child victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and child victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children.

Article 8

2. In establishing an IPU as referred to in paragraph (1), it shall be guided by the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation regulates protection efforts for women and child victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and child victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Batu Bara Regency.

2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Batu Bara.
5. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Child protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering as a result of Violence and/or threat of Violence.
13. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
14. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
15. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to the region of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
18. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or Victims of acts of Violence.

19. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
20. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service unit services in reports/providing complaint handling services, health services, Social Rehabilitation, enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER VI

MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS

Article 9

MSS for Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence include services for:
a. handling complaints/reports of victims of violence against women and children;
b. health services for women and children victims of violence;
c. Social rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; d. law enforcement and legal aid for women and children victims of violence; ande. repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. 13. The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation regulates protection efforts for women and child victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and child victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation regulates protection efforts for women and child victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and child victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children.
